BC_description: The event handling API for queue and queue-derived objects (queue, priorityQueue, cargo, cargoQueue) has changed. Previously, event handlers for events such as 'drain', 'saturated', 'unsaturated', 'empty', and 'error' were set via property assignment (e.g., q.drain = callback;). This is no longer supported. Now, each supported event is managed through a method on the queue instance: - To register a handler, call q.<event>(callback) (e.g., q.drain(callback);). - To await the next occurrence of an event, call await q.<event>();. - Setting q.<event> by property assignment (e.g., q.drain = callback;) will have no effect; the property is now a function used for event registration or promise-based handling. The full impacted set of events, as evidenced by the code, is: ['drain', 'saturated', 'unsaturated', 'empty', 'error']. Event methods must be called as functions to set handlers or await events. All code relying on property assignment for queue event handling must be updated accordingly. The change applies only to these explicit events on queue and related classes; no unrelated APIs are affected.
Adaptation_method:
Update event handling on queue objects as follows.

Before:
q.drain = callback;
q.saturated = callback;
q.empty = callback;
q.error = callback;
q.unsaturated = callback;

After:
q.drain(callback); // register handler for drain
q.saturated(callback); // register handler for saturated
q.empty(callback); // register handler for empty
q.error(callback); // register handler for error
q.unsaturated(callback); // register handler for unsaturated

To wait for an event instead of handling via callback (e.g., for one-time use):
await q.drain(); // resolves when drain event occurs
await q.error(); // resolves when error event occurs

Direct assignment (q.drain = ...) will no longer work. Use the method call forms only.
